status: pilot: 10 of 83 aquarium-scope species; care.ts untouched

species.name: Betta splendens

sources.label: Moderate
sources.why: territorial, needs own tank, careful tankmates, obesity-prone; water flexible
no label; says first-timers can succeed with preparation (5 gal, heater, filter, cycling); notes narrow temp range and fin rot/ich
titled best beginner pet fish but not called easy; needs heater and 5-10+ gal; illness mostly from poor maintenance

species.reason: Labels split 2/1/1, but both beginner-leaning sources make success conditional on heater, cycled 5+ gal tank and maintenance, which fits level 2 (a beginner often loses it in a bowl); keep 2.

species.name: Otocinclus affinis / vittatus

sources.why: starvation not disease; wild-caught, fasted 3-6 weeks before sale; needs mature tank with biofilm/algae

sources.label: Moderate
sources.why: simple husbandry but needs mature biofilm tank and high import mortality

species.reason: Two independent sources agree on established tank plus diet/import losses; web search also showed other guides split Easy vs Moderate (not opened). Seriously Fish oto URL returned 404.

species.name: Pangio kuhlii

sources.label: Easy
sources.why: flexible water, compatible; needs a group and a lid (jumps)

sources.label: Beginner (Easy)
sources.why: hardy, wide pH/GH, peaceful; group of 3-6, hiding spots, target-feed (nocturnal)

sources.label: Easy
sources.why: label Easy but text says scaleless, prone to skin disease, needs stable water, not best for hardy low-maintenance beginners

species.reason: All three label Easy; Fishkeeping World caveat (scaleless, disease-prone) noted but does not change the level.

species.name: Siamese algae eater (Crossocheilus oblongus)

sources.label: Easy
sources.why: peaceful, hardy, eats most foods; 20+ gal, heater, lid
no label; hardy across 68-80F, pH 6-8; needs 50-55 gal, semi-aggressive to own kind, adults stop eating algae

sources.label: Moderate
sources.why: URL is the genus page covering seven Crossocheilus species, all Moderate; no stated reason, hints at groups of 6+ and large tanks; not specific to C. oblongus

species.reason: Two sources read Easy (hardy; size/tank and aggression are the demands); Seriously Fish Moderate is a genus-level page, so split is explainable; keep 1.

species.name: Hillstream loach (Sewellia / Beaufortia)

sources.label: Moderate
sources.why: needs a well-established tank and stable water; clean, fast, oxygenated flow, 68-75 F

sources.label: Easy
sources.why: called hardy, but also fussy about water conditions (clean, oxygenated, strong flow)
relatively easy only while parameters stay stable; needs high oxygen, cool water, frequent large water changes

species.reason: Labels split (Moderate vs Easy) but every page's stated reasons are flow, oxygen and stable water, which fits intermediate.

species.name: Neon tetra

sources.label: Easy
sources.why: hardy, low care needs, tolerates a range of water
peaceful, ideal for a beginner community tank; quarantine for neon tetra disease

species.reason: Two independent pages say beginner-friendly; only caveat is disease/quarantine.

species.name: Discus (Symphysodon)

sources.why: best for devoted or experienced keepers; needs attention to water quality, pH, hardness, diet; easier now with captive-raised fish

sources.label: Specialist community (compatibility field)
sources.why: soft acidic water, RO suggested, very sensitive to metals/organics, large tank, group care

sources.label: Difficulty of care: 9
sources.why: sensitive to water changes and pollutants, disease-prone; keeping one alive a year counts as success (wild-type Heckel)

species.reason: Two pages read expert-level; LiveAquaria softens it for captive-bred stock, so split is explainable by wild vs captive-bred.

species.name: Guppy (Poecilia reticulata)

sources.label: Easy
sources.why: peaceful, adaptable, hardier than most fish, still needs consistent conditions
described as hardy and surprisingly easy if needs are met (teaser text only, no formal rating)

species.reason: Both pages call it hardy and beginner-friendly; Tankarium has no formal label, so only two weak-to-moderate sources.

species.name: mandarin dragonet

sources.label: Intermediate
sources.why: label says Intermediate but text says demanding and not for beginners: specific diet, live copepods, wean onto prepared food 'extremely difficult', needs 30+ gal with 75 lb live rock

sources.label: Difficult
sources.why: slow, live-food feeder hard to acclimate; only for long-established tank with copepod population
once expert-only, now 'relatively easy' with captive-bred fish trained to frozen food; wild-caught still starve without live copepods

species.reason: Split is explained: wild-caught specialist diet is the killer; captive-bred eases it, but 2 of 3 sources still call it hard/not for beginners, so keep 3.

species.name: freshwater angelfish

sources.label: Easy (common varieties: silver, zebra, platinum, marble); Moderate for altum, koi, albino
sources.why: hardy, beginner-friendly common strains; moderate only for rarer varieties
no explicit label; tank-raised are hardy and not picky, but need large tank (80 gal for group), regular maintenance, aggression/eats small fish

species.reason: Only 2 pages opened; hardiness points to 1, the moderate reading is about tank size and temperament, not loss rate. Keep 1.
